summary: Postinstall and require-time dropper fetches and executes remote binary from obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts with DNS-TXT fallback
details: beaver-ui-card-large@12.4.3 ships a setup.js that runs both from the package's postinstall lifecycle hook and unconditionally from index.js (the declared main entry) via a try/catch require of./setup. On execution it assembles destination hostnames from split string arrays (e.g. "oob-wor"+"ker.cf"+"99-9b3.wor"+"kers"+".dev") to rotate across five Cloudflare Workers subdomains under workers.dev and fallback hosts under dl.well1.site (tin, tina, ldr, win). It downloads a platform-specific binary via https.get, writes it to /var/tmp/.cache_<hex> on Unix or %TEMP%/dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe on Windows (cover name imitating a Microsoft diagnostic tool), chmods it 0755, and launches it detached with stdio redirected to /dev/null. A stamp file gates re-runs on a 6-hour TTL. If HTTP retrieval fails, the code falls back to a DNS-TXT covert channel: it resolves TXT records on c.<domain> for a chunk count then i.<domain> for indexed chunks, base64-decodes and concatenates them to reassemble the binary payload, bypassing HTTP-based egress inspection. setup.js also runs execSync('powershell...') on Windows. The fetched binary is unpinned, unverified, delivered from anonymous infrastructure whose hostnames are obfuscated at the source level, and executed on every install and every require of the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
